prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one portrait-format review illustration for a Slay the Spire 2 female-character appearance MOD; a new design, not a finished game asset.

Primary request: Create ONE unmistakably human-faced adult woman as Ironclad, the last soldier of the Ironclads. She is beautiful, compelling and strong through her composure and chosen action. Depict a private moment between battles: she steadies her weight against her sword, exhales slowly, and tries to contain the cursed flame in her other hand. Power is pressing against her will. Her face, hands and grounded posture tell this story before the armor details do.

Input images:
Image 1 is the official 2025 Ironclad illustration, decoded frame040 from Mega Crit's pose-reference GIF. Use only its meaningful equipment motifs: a pointed gold-bronze full-face mask, broad simple shoulder plates, dark torso, silver blade and angular dark guard. It contains no human photograph. Do not reproduce its covered face, pose, red backdrop or IRONCLAD lettering.
Image 2 is an official Steam co-op screenshot. Use ONLY the sword-bearing Ironclad in the foreground at the left for the practical segmented armor, covered dark torso, muted red-brown underclothes, boots and sense of weight. Ignore all other characters, monsters, throne, scenery, cards and interface. Both images are equipment references, not identity or face-preservation targets. Redesign the person into the clearly visible human woman requested here.

Subject: A naturally proportioned adult female soldier with an athletic, believable body under useful armor, neither a hulking caricature nor an exaggerated fashion figure. Clearly visible human cheeks, nose, mouth and expressive amber-brown eyes; a refined, attractive face with a firm brow and a little fatigue. Silver-gray hair, short enough to clear the shoulders, swept back with a few loose strands by the cheek. Human ears, no horns. Her brow and jaw carry quiet effort, but she remains lucid and composed. Her eyes focus on her own flame, never on the viewer; lips slightly parted on a controlled breath, without a smile, pout or seductive expression.

Action and composition: One complete head-to-boots figure in a three-quarter view, both feet and the entire sword comfortably inside the frame. Use an asymmetrical, physically plausible stance: feet about hip-width apart, one knee slightly bent, weight supported through a planted heel, pelvis beneath the ribcage, shoulders lowering as she breathes. A gloved hand grips the upright sword hilt beside her body, its blade tip touching the stone ground as a temporary brace. Her other hand is bare at chest height, fingers drawing inward around one small, restless orange-red flame coming from her palm. Keep this hand and all its fingers legible, angled toward herself, as though she is containing an involuntary flare rather than showing a spell to an audience. Make the line from her gaze to her fingers and the opposing weight of the sword easy to read. No combat swing or pin-up stance.

Equipment and materials: Simple, functional gold-bronze/copper armor with broad shoulder plates, articulated forearm guards, practical waist tassets and armored boots, over a fully covered charcoal torso and muted red-brown trousers. Allow joints to bend; use a few necessary seams, rivets and worn edges rather than ornament. The torso protection is a continuous practical shape, without molded breast cups or a corset waist. Keep the silver broad longsword and recognizable angular dark guard. Her original full-size, pointed gold-bronze face mask is temporarily stored at the outer hip in a plain leather carrying loop, facing outward enough to read the original tapered plates and narrow eye slits. It must still look usable over her face, not like a tiny decorative charm or an extra head. Leave her actual face entirely uncovered. This storage arrangement and her human appearance are MOD interpretations, not claims about official lore.

Style/medium: Polished anime-inspired 2D character illustration, with attractive human facial design, confident clean contours, lively simplified color shapes and restrained painterly material shading. Crisp readable silhouettes, soft clear light on skin and silver hair, interesting rhythmic edges. Beauty comes from resolve, the expressive face and the purposeful hands. Keep armor substantial but not crude or ugly; keep skin luminous without turning her into a glamorous princess. No copying Silent's face, hood, outfit or pose.

Scene/backdrop and light: A quiet, pale smoky-gray backdrop and a small suggestion of stone under her feet, leaving generous breathing room around the full silhouette. Soft neutral light keeps the face and joints readable; the single small flame adds a restrained warm reflection to the fingers, cheek and adjacent bronze. Group detail around the face, hands, sword guard and stored mask. Background is opaque, not alpha-transparent. The flame is a tense localized accent, not a wall of fire.

Constraints: Exactly one woman and one sword; two coherent arms and hands; anatomically credible knees, hips, elbows and grip. Face, silver-gray hair, stored mask, useful armor, sword and contained flame must all be visible in the same illustration. No text, signature, logo, watermark, interface, collage, inset portraits or lineup. Do not hide her face, use red hair, a gown, gold filigree, jewelry, crown, a large red cape, revealing armor, cleavage, bare abdomen or thighs, exaggerated muscles, breasts or hips. Do not turn her into a cheerful berserker, a generic elegant sword princess, a grimacing monster, or a viewer-facing beauty pose. No companions, enemies, blood or graphic injuries.
